Experian Becomes First Personal Finance App Integrated with Google Gemini
summary:
Today, Experian, the global data and technology company, and Google announced a strategic collaboration that makes Experian the first personal finance app integrated with Google Gemini, expanding Experian's reach to one of the world's largest AI platforms and creating a new way for consumers to discover, access, and engage with Experian through conversational AI.
“Consumers increasingly expect to engage across the experiences and platforms that are part of their everyday lives,” said Jeff Softley, CEO of Experian North America.
“Our collaboration with Google delivers on that expectation, giving our existing members another way to engage with Experian while introducing us to consumers who may be discovering Experian for the first time. By bringing consumer-permissioned Experian credit insights into Gemini, we can help consumers better understand their credit and put their own information to work for them, in addition to the products, services, and experiences we power directly for our clients.”
Consumers in the United States will be able to connect with Experian in Gemini through a consumer-authorized experience and ask questions about their credit. Existing Experian members can connect their accounts, while consumers who discover Experian through Gemini can join Experian at no cost. They can also access their FICO® credit rating and key factors influencing it.
As AI assistants increasingly become part of how people navigate everyday decisions, Experian is extending trusted financial information into an emerging consumer channel while keeping consumers in control of whether their Experian information is connected and used. The collaboration also creates a new point of discovery for Experian, allowing consumers already using Gemini to connect with Experian, where they can access a broader range of financial products, services, and capabilities through the Experian app or website.
Turning Credit Information into Understanding
Consumers can ask Gemini questions about their Experian credit information and receive personalized responses designed to make that information easier to understand.
For example, a user can ask, “@Experian, what’s my credit rating?” and be prompted to connect directly with Experian to receive their credit rating within the Gemini experience. They can also ask about key factors influencing their credit, giving them additional context about where they stand and what may be affecting their credit profile.
Rather than simply viewing static information, consumers can ask questions in a conversational experience that combines Experian’s trusted credit data with Gemini’s AI capabilities to help make credit information easier to understand.
Consumers who want to view their FICO® Score 8 will continue to access it directly through the Experian website or app, where they can access a broader range of products, services, and capabilities designed to help them manage their financial lives and find more ways to save time and money.
How It Works
Connecting to Google Gemini’s Connect App ecosystem is designed to be simple, secure, and consumer controlled.
Users sign in to their Google account and open Gemini. From the Personal Intelligence menu, they can navigate to Connected Apps, select Experian, and choose to link and authorize access to their Experian account. Users also have the ability to tag “@Experian” to connect with the Experian app within a chat when asking a credit-related question.
Existing Experian members can authorize access to their Experian account, while consumers who are new to Experian can join at no cost and establish an Experian membership.
After securely authenticating, consumers can ask Gemini questions about their Experian credit information, including their FICO® credit rating and the key factors influencing it. Consumers can manage their connected app settings through Google’s Personal Intelligence settings at any time.
Expanding How Consumers Discover and Access Experian
The collaboration builds on Experian’s long track record of consumer innovation and advances its strategy of giving consumers more ways to engage where they choose.
As consumers increasingly use AI-powered assistants alongside apps, websites, and other digital experiences, Experian is expanding the ways consumers can access and engage with trusted financial information. The Gemini integration gives Experian another way to reach consumers, both existing members and people discovering Experian for the first time, through an AI platform that is increasingly part of consumers' everyday lives.
Gemini becomes another channel in Experian's broader consumer ecosystem, complementing the products and services it provides directly and the experiences it powers for financial institutions and other clients. Together, these experiences give consumers more ways to access Experian information, insights, and capabilities throughout their financial lives.
The companies also plan to build on the collaboration over time, expanding the Experian capabilities consumers can access through Gemini—such as subscription cancellation, which could help consumers save on unwanted subscriptions they currently pay for.

summary:

A field that reflects exactly what the payments industry looks like right now: competitive, innovative and showing no signs of slowing down.
 
This is what nearly 20 years of industry recognition looks like when the industry itself keeps raising the bar.
 
Emma Banymandhub, CEO of The Payments Association, said: "The PAY360 Awards have been recognising excellence in payments for nearly two decades, and this year's record entry numbers are a real statement of intent from the industry. title: Trade Tech Solutions Enters New Phase of Growth, 2 Million Users Strong
summary:
With more than 2 million users, over 1 million active accounts each month, more than 200 million dollars in client revenues processed through its infrastructure each year and 100 million dollars in payouts processed to date, Trade Tech Solutions is consolidating its position as the technology layer beneath a large share of the prop and broker market.
The proprietary trading industry has grown quickly, and the technology underneath it has had to grow with it. Prop firms have moved well beyond forex and CFDs, brokers are launching their own challenge-based products, and traders now judge a firm as much on execution, platform stability and payout reliability as on its marketing. Behind that shift is a quieter question for operators: whether their infrastructure can keep pace.
Trade Tech Solutions has reached a point that answers it in scale. The company has surpassed 2 million users, the individual traders holding accounts with the firms running on its technology, and has processed more than 100 million dollars in payouts to date. Its infrastructure also handles over 1 million active accounts every month and more than 200 million dollars in client revenues each year, processed on behalf of the 85+ prop firms it supports across 180+ regions, spanning forex, CFDs, futures, cryptocurrencies, sports and prediction markets.
The milestone marks a change in what the company is. Trade Tech Solutions has grown from a prop firm technology vendor into the operating backbone for a substantial part of the market, with payments, risk, compliance, CRM and back-office workflows connected in one system rather than stitched together from separate tools.
One connected system, not a stack of parts
The trading industry's technology requirements have become more demanding as the products themselves have diversified. Firms now need infrastructure that supports multiple asset classes, connects with established trading platforms, processes payments across many regions and gives operators clear visibility into trader activity, risk exposure and account performance, all at once.
Trade Tech Solutions is built to deliver those functions through a single operating environment rather than a collection of integrations. The platform supports more than 20 trading platforms, including MT4, MT5, cTrader, Match-Trader, NinjaTrader and Tradovate, and can support prediction markets trading through Match-Trader integration, allowing firms to introduce event-based products alongside their existing offerings.
"Trading businesses are no longer working within one clearly defined product category," said Stefano M., Partnership Manager at Trade Tech Solutions. "Operators want infrastructure that can support different trading models while keeping technology, risk management, payments and customer operations connected. That flexibility is becoming central to how firms plan for growth."
Built for brokers as well as prop firms
While much of the prop sector's attention has focused on challenge providers, the same infrastructure requirements now apply to brokers building their own prop-style offerings. Trade Tech Solutions positions its technology for both, giving established brokers a route into challenge-based products without assembling a separate technology stack to run them.
For new entrants, the time required to launch a trading business affects both operating costs and the ability to act on market opportunities. For established firms, replacing legacy infrastructure raises concerns about downtime, data fragmentation and disruption to existing traders. Trade Tech Solutions offers migration in as little as 48 hours and can have new firms live in as little as seven days, depending on scope, which lowers both barriers at once.
The platform pairs that speed with breadth: customer management, trader dashboards, real-time risk monitoring, checkout, KYC and AML integrations, and back-office operations, all handled within the same environment. Firms can introduce new products without running a separate system for each stage of the customer and trading lifecycle.
Payments and payouts across 180+ regions
Access to funds is one of the clearest markers of a well-run prop operation and one of the most common sources of trader frustration when it goes wrong. Trade Tech Solutions' infrastructure connects to more than 80 payment processors across 180+ regions, giving operators flexibility in how they handle deposits and payout requests and reducing dependence on any single provider.
Payouts are semi-automated and include a manual approval step, an additional control before funds are released. Traders can track the relevant rules, limits and payout requests through a real-time dashboard, so the process stays visible on both sides.
Visibility as the foundation of trust
As the sector has matured, traders have grown more attentive to the operational detail behind the firms they choose. Execution quality, platform stability, account visibility and payout processes all shape whether a firm earns their confidence.
Trade Tech Solutions gives firms the tools to display challenge rules, account performance, risk exposure and relevant trading information through a centralised dashboard. All trading accounts supported through these programmes are simulated, with firms managing the related rules and workflows through the platform. For operators, the same visibility supports more consistent risk management and makes it easier to identify irregularities across accounts and trading activity.
"Technology has to serve both sides of the trading relationship," Stefano M. added. "Firms need visibility across their operations, and traders need clear information about their accounts, rules and requests. Connecting those functions creates a more transparent environment for everyone involved."
Proven across the sector
Trade Tech Solutions' technology is currently used by 85+ prop firms, including Goat Funded Trader and Goat Funded Futures. The two brands show how a single infrastructure can support different trading programmes while keeping account management, trading platforms, risk controls and payouts connected across both.
With more than 2 million users across its network, over 1 million active accounts each month, more than 200 million dollars in client revenues processed through its infrastructure each year and 100 million dollars in payouts processed to date, Trade Tech Solutions has moved from being one vendor among many into an established infrastructure layer for the trading industry. Its growth reflects a broader shift among brokers and prop firms towards integrated technology that supports multiple products, regional requirements and operational processes without relying on fragmented systems.

Equifax Launches Two New Intelligence Solutions to Help Businesses Mitigate Automated Fraud
summary:
Equifax® is expanding its fraud prevention capabilities with the launch of two new intelligence solutions: Signal Score for Email and Signal Score for Device. The new Signal Scores are designed to help e-commerce retailers, financial institutions and telecommunication companies protect their digital platforms - such as online checkout lanes, new account sign-up portals and mobile ordering apps - against sophisticated fraud networks and automated threats.
 

"Businesses can no longer rely on static snapshots of customers to stop fraud," said Ajay Guru, Senior Vice President and General Manager, Identity & Fraud Services at Equifax. "Leveraging our unique differentiated data, these new solutions are designed to deliver a trust score in real time, giving our customers a better view of a user and helping them to mitigate fraud more quickly."
 
As digital fraud grows increasingly complex, traditional checks are no longer enough to deter automated threats because they cannot see behind the digital blind spots created by VPNs and emulators. Organizations need real-time intelligence to instantly detect sophisticated tactics like script-driven account farming, location spoofing and synthetic identity fraud before they impact the business.
 
The new Signal Score for Email and Signal Score for Device solutions are designed to use proprietary Equifax data to evaluate risk instantly at the start of a transaction, keeping the experience simple and secure for legitimate consumers. Unlike traditional industry tools that rely on static global networks or lagging database files, the solutions leverage Equifax non-public, first-party sourced data and unique identity linkage to instantly connect digital session behaviors with trusted, real-world consumer profiles.
 
Translating Email and Device Signals into Immediate, Actionable Trust Scores
 


Signal Score for Email: Evaluates an email address in real time. It assesses the age of the account, its history and its risk level to determine if the digital identifier is trustworthy.
Signal Score for Device: Analyzes the computer or phone used in a transaction. It connects device details, location data and network information to validate the electronic instrument to the user.
 
The two new Signal Scores connect directly to a company's existing fraud prevention or case management systems through Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), making it easy for businesses to enhance current fraud stacks. Companies can use both tools together or pick one to fill a specific data intelligence gap. Designed specifically for internal fraud and risk teams, the new tools deliver faster, actionable data at critical entry points like new account sign-ups and checkouts.
 

"Fraud can happen at any step of an online interaction," added Guru. "Our unique data and tools give companies what they need to stop criminals without adding slow, extra steps for valid customers."
 
By spotting high-risk users early, companies can reduce manual review costs while providing a faster experience for honest consumers.
 
In addition to the new Signal Scores, Equifax offers Consumer Insights, which uses basic information to help businesses assess fraud risk and payment ability and help compliance and security teams prevent account takeovers.
